**[MERIDIAN CASUALTY INSURANCE COMPANY]{.underline}**

**[Regulatory Filing Archive]{.underline}**

**Prior Colorado Division of Insurance Objection Correspondence**

**Compiled by:** Alicia Brennan, Regulatory Filing Analyst **Date of Compilation:** January 15, 2025

**Purpose of This Compilation**

The following two objection letters were received from the Colorado Division of Insurance in connection with prior form filings submitted by Meridian Casualty Insurance Company (NAIC Code: 29847). They are compiled here for reference in connection with the independent regulatory review of Form MCP-2025-01 (Meridian Commercial Property Coverage Form, Edition Date: January 2025) by outside counsel Hargrove & Calloway LLP.

Filing MERI-2021-003, objected to on July 14, 2021, concerned a deficiency in the nonrenewal notice period contained in a commercial property endorsement form. Filing MERI-2023-007, objected to on March 22, 2023, concerned the absence of mandatory wildfire coverage disclosure language from a commercial property endorsement form. Both objections were issued by the Property & Casualty Forms Review Unit of the Colorado Division of Insurance under the authority of Deputy Commissioner Janet Winslow.

These objections were subsequently resolved and the corrected filings approved. However, the issues identified in these letters should be cross-referenced against the new proprietary form to ensure no recurrence. The transition from an ISO-based commercial property program to a fully proprietary form increases the risk that Colorado-specific requirements addressed in prior endorsement filings may be inadvertently omitted from the new form. Accordingly, both letters are included in the materials being transmitted to outside counsel for the independent compliance review engagement.

**Distribution:**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Recipient**                       **Title / Affiliation**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Patricia Voss, Esq.                 General Counsel, Meridian Casualty Insurance Company

  David Kaminski                      Vice President, Regulatory Compliance, Meridian Casualty Insurance Company

  Rebecca Sung, Esq.                  Hargrove & Calloway LLP
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Meridian Casualty Insurance Company** 200 West Adams Street, Suite 3200 Chicago, IL 60606

**Hargrove & Calloway LLP** 1750 Welton Street, Suite 400 Denver, CO 80202

**--- OBJECTION LETTER #1 ---** **Filing MERI-2021-003** **Nonrenewal Notice Period Deficiency**

**COLORADO DIVISION OF INSURANCE** Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA) 1560 Broadway, Suite 850 Denver, CO 80202

*Office of the Commissioner* Michael R. Delacroix, Commissioner of Insurance

July 14, 2021

**Via SERFF Electronic Correspondence and First-Class Mail**

Patricia Voss, Esq. General Counsel Meridian Casualty Insurance Company 200 West Adams Street, Suite 3200 Chicago, IL 60606

**RE:** Filing Objection --- SERFF Filing No. MERI-2021-003; Meridian Casualty Insurance Company (NAIC Code: 29847); Commercial Property Endorsement Form

Dear Ms. Voss:

The Colorado Division of Insurance (the \"Division\") has completed its review of the above-referenced filing submitted by Meridian Casualty Insurance Company (\"Meridian\") through the System for Electronic Rates & Forms Filing (\"SERFF\"). The filing was received on June 7, 2021, and was assigned to the Division\'s Property & Casualty Forms Review Unit under the supervision of Deputy Commissioner for Property & Casualty Janet Winslow. The filing was reviewed for compliance with applicable provisions of Title 10 of the Colorado Revised Statutes and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder at 3 CCR 702-4.

Upon completion of this review, the Division has identified a deficiency in the filed endorsement form that requires correction before the filing can be approved for use in this state. The deficiency is described below.

**IDENTIFICATION OF DEFICIENCY --- NONRENEWAL NOTICE PERIOD**

The filed commercial property endorsement form contains a \"Cancellation and Nonrenewal\" provision (Section VII, paragraph D) that states, in pertinent part:

> \"If we elect not to renew this policy, we will mail written notice of nonrenewal to the first Named Insured shown in the Declarations at least 30 days before the expiration date of this policy.\"

This provision is deficient under Colorado law. Section 10-4-403(1)(b) of the Colorado Revised Statutes requires that, for commercial property insurance policies, the insurer must provide written notice of nonrenewal to the named insured **at least forty-five (45) days** before the policy expiration date. The relevant statutory language provides:

> \"An insurer that elects not to renew a policy of commercial property insurance shall mail or deliver to the named insured, at the address shown in the policy, written notice of the insurer\'s intention not to renew. Such notice shall be mailed or delivered not less than forty-five days before the expiration date of the policy.\" --- C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b)

The filed form provides only thirty (30) days\' advance notice of nonrenewal, which is fifteen (15) days shorter than the statutory minimum of forty-five (45) days mandated by C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b). As drafted, this provision would violate the insured\'s statutory right to adequate advance notice of nonrenewal and is therefore non-compliant with Colorado law.

The 30-day nonrenewal notice period in the filed form is inconsistent with, and less favorable to the insured than, the 45-day minimum notice period mandated by C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b). This deficiency renders the form non-compliant with Colorado law as currently enacted. The Division notes that the 45-day requirement applies to all commercial property policies issued, delivered, or renewed in the State of Colorado, regardless of premium size, policy limits, or insured classification. This is a consumer protection provision that cannot be shortened or waived by contract, endorsement, or agreement between the parties.

**REQUIRED CORRECTIVE ACTION**

The Division requires Meridian to amend the nonrenewal notice provision in the filed endorsement form to provide at least forty-five (45) days\' advance written notice before the policy expiration date, consistent with the requirements of C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b). The Division suggests the following corrective language, which the Division would find acceptable:

> \"If we elect not to renew this policy, we will mail written notice of nonrenewal to the first Named Insured shown in the Declarations at least forty-five (45) days before the expiration date of this policy.\"

Meridian may propose alternative language that achieves compliance with the statute, provided that the notice period is not less than forty-five (45) days.

The corrected endorsement form must be resubmitted through SERFF as a revised filing within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of this objection letter --- i.e., no later than **August 13, 2021**. Failure to respond to this objection within thirty (30) days may result in the filing being closed with a disposition of \"Rejected --- No Response\" in accordance with the Division\'s filing review procedures.

**CLOSING**

Should Meridian wish to discuss this objection or seek clarification regarding the applicable statutory requirements, please contact the Division\'s Property & Casualty Forms Review Unit at (303) 894-7499, ext. 4412, or by email at dora*pnc*formreview@state.co.us. Staff are available to assist with questions regarding corrective filings.

Please note that this objection letter addresses only the nonrenewal notice period deficiency identified above. All other provisions of Filing MERI-2021-003 remain subject to the Division\'s ongoing review, and the Division reserves the right to raise additional objections or request additional information as the review continues.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. The Division appreciates Meridian\'s cooperation in ensuring that all forms filed for use in Colorado comply with the requirements of Colorado law.

Respectfully,

COLORADO DIVISION OF INSURANCE

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Janet Winslow Deputy Commissioner for Property & Casualty Colorado Division of Insurance Department of Regulatory Agencies 1560 Broadway, Suite 850 Denver, CO 80202

cc: Michael R. Delacroix, Commissioner of Insurance SERFF Filing Record --- MERI-2021-003

**--- OBJECTION LETTER #2 ---** **Filing MERI-2023-007** **Wildfire Coverage Disclosure Deficiency**

**COLORADO DIVISION OF INSURANCE** Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA) 1560 Broadway, Suite 850 Denver, CO 80202

*Office of the Commissioner* Michael R. Delacroix, Commissioner of Insurance

March 22, 2023

**Via SERFF Electronic Correspondence and First-Class Mail**

Patricia Voss, Esq. General Counsel Meridian Casualty Insurance Company 200 West Adams Street, Suite 3200 Chicago, IL 60606

**RE:** Filing Objection --- SERFF Filing No. MERI-2023-007; Meridian Casualty Insurance Company (NAIC Code: 29847); Commercial Property Endorsement Form --- Wildfire Coverage Disclosure Deficiency

Dear Ms. Voss:

The Colorado Division of Insurance (the \"Division\") has completed its review of the above-referenced filing submitted by Meridian Casualty Insurance Company (\"Meridian\") through the System for Electronic Rates & Forms Filing (\"SERFF\"). The filing was received on February 14, 2023, and was reviewed by the Division\'s Property & Casualty Forms Review Unit for compliance with applicable provisions of Title 10 of the Colorado Revised Statutes and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

Upon completion of this review, the Division has identified a deficiency in the filed endorsement form that requires correction before the filing can be approved for use in the State of Colorado. The Division notes that wildfire-related regulatory requirements have been a particular area of focus for the Division in light of Colorado\'s significant and growing wildfire risk exposure. The Marshall Fire of December 30, 2021, which destroyed more than 1,000 structures in Boulder County and resulted in insured losses exceeding \$2 billion, underscored the critical importance of ensuring that policyholders are fully and clearly informed about the scope and limitations of their wildfire coverage. The Colorado General Assembly and this Division have taken legislative and regulatory action to strengthen wildfire coverage transparency, and compliance with these requirements is a priority in all form reviews.

The specific deficiency identified is described below.

**IDENTIFICATION OF DEFICIENCY --- MISSING WILDFIRE COVERAGE DISCLOSURE**

Section 10-4-110.5 of the Colorado Revised Statutes mandates that commercial property insurance policies sold, issued, delivered, or renewed in the State of Colorado must include specific disclosure language regarding wildfire coverage. This statute was enacted to ensure that commercial property policyholders receive clear and conspicuous information about their wildfire coverage status, and it applies to all commercial property policies regardless of whether the underlying policy covers or excludes wildfire losses.

Under C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5, the required wildfire coverage disclosure must address each of the following elements:

> \(1\) Whether the policy provides coverage for losses caused by wildfire;
>
> \(2\) Any wildfire-specific sublimits that apply to wildfire losses, if applicable, including the dollar amount of any such sublimit;
>
> \(3\) Any wildfire-specific exclusions or limitations that apply to wildfire losses, including any conditions or circumstances under which wildfire coverage may not apply;
>
> \(4\) Any wildfire-specific deductibles that differ from the standard policy deductible, including the dollar amount or percentage basis of any such deductible; and
>
> \(5\) A clear and conspicuous statement informing the policyholder of their wildfire coverage status in plain language that is readily understandable to a person without specialized insurance knowledge.

The Division has reviewed the filed endorsement form and has determined that it does not contain any wildfire-specific disclosure, notice, or informational provisions. While the Division acknowledges that fire coverage is included within the general fire peril of the policy\'s covered causes of loss provisions, C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5 requires a separate, specific disclosure regarding wildfire coverage that is distinct from the general insuring agreement or covered causes of loss provisions. The inclusion of fire as a covered peril does not, standing alone, satisfy the disclosure requirements of the statute.

The absence of the mandated wildfire coverage disclosure language renders the filed form non-compliant with C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5. This disclosure requirement is mandatory and applies regardless of whether the policy covers wildfire losses --- the insured must be informed of their wildfire coverage status through explicit disclosure language in the policy form or in a mandatory notice accompanying the policy. A policyholder reading the filed form would not find any specific information about wildfire coverage, wildfire sublimits, wildfire exclusions, or wildfire deductibles, and would therefore be unable to ascertain their wildfire coverage status from the policy documents as required by law.

The Colorado legislature enacted C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5 to address the demonstrated need for wildfire coverage transparency in a state that has experienced catastrophic wildfire events with increasing frequency and severity. Compliance with this requirement has been a Division priority in form reviews since the statute\'s enactment, and the Division expects all insurers filing commercial property forms in Colorado to incorporate the mandated wildfire disclosure language.

**REQUIRED CORRECTIVE ACTION**

The Division requires Meridian to add wildfire-specific disclosure language to the filed form that complies with all elements of C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5 as described above. The required disclosure may be incorporated in either of the following manners:

> \(a\) **Directly into the policy form** in a clearly labeled section (e.g., \"WILDFIRE COVERAGE DISCLOSURE\" or \"IMPORTANT NOTICE REGARDING WILDFIRE COVERAGE\"), set apart from surrounding policy provisions and clearly identifiable by the policyholder; or
>
> \(b\) **As a mandatory notice or endorsement** that must accompany the policy at issuance and at each renewal, provided that the notice or endorsement is referenced in the policy form and is included in the filing as a required attachment.

Regardless of the format selected, the wildfire disclosure language must be written in plain language, must be conspicuous, and must be set apart from surrounding text. The Division requires that the disclosure be printed in a font size no smaller than 10-point type and recommends the use of bold or otherwise emphasized formatting to ensure conspicuousness.

The Division directs Meridian\'s attention to the sample wildfire disclosure language available in the Division\'s form filing guidance manual, specifically Colorado DOI Form Filing Guidance, Section 7.3 --- Wildfire Disclosures, which provides model language and formatting guidance that the Division has determined to be compliant with the statute. Meridian may use the model language verbatim or may propose alternative language, provided that all required statutory elements are addressed.

The corrected endorsement form, including the wildfire disclosure language, must be resubmitted through SERFF as a revised filing within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of this objection letter --- i.e., no later than **April 21, 2023**. Failure to respond to this objection within thirty (30) days may result in the filing being closed with a disposition of \"Rejected --- No Response\" in accordance with the Division\'s filing review procedures.

**CLOSING**

Should Meridian wish to discuss this objection or seek clarification regarding the wildfire disclosure requirements under C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5, please contact the Division\'s Property & Casualty Forms Review Unit at (303) 894-7499, ext. 4412, or by email at dora*pnc*formreview@state.co.us. Staff are available to assist with questions regarding corrective filings and the application of the wildfire disclosure statute.

The Division takes wildfire coverage transparency seriously and encourages all insurers operating in Colorado to proactively review their existing Colorado-filed forms for compliance with C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5. Given the ongoing wildfire risk in this state, the Division considers complete and accurate wildfire disclosure to be essential to protecting the interests of Colorado policyholders.

Please note that this objection letter addresses only the wildfire coverage disclosure deficiency identified above. All other provisions of Filing MERI-2023-007 remain subject to the Division\'s ongoing review, and the Division reserves the right to raise additional objections or request additional information as the review continues.

Thank you for your cooperation in this matter.

Respectfully,

COLORADO DIVISION OF INSURANCE

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Janet Winslow Deputy Commissioner for Property & Casualty Colorado Division of Insurance Department of Regulatory Agencies 1560 Broadway, Suite 850 Denver, CO 80202

cc: Michael R. Delacroix, Commissioner of Insurance SERFF Filing Record --- MERI-2023-007

**[INTERNAL COMPLIANCE NOTES]{.underline}**

**[Disposition of Prior Objections]{.underline}**

**Prepared by:** Alicia Brennan, Regulatory Filing Analyst **Date:** January 15, 2025 **Classification:** Internal --- Attorney-Client Privileged / Work Product

**Disposition of Filing MERI-2021-003 --- Nonrenewal Notice Period**

**Objection Received:** July 14, 2021

**Issue Identified:** The filed commercial property endorsement contained a nonrenewal notice period of thirty (30) days. The Colorado Division of Insurance objected on the grounds that C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b) requires a minimum nonrenewal notice period of forty-five (45) days for commercial property insurance policies. The 30-day provision was fifteen (15) days shorter than the statutory minimum.

**Corrective Action Taken:** The Cancellation and Nonrenewal provision of the endorsement was revised to provide forty-five (45) days\' advance written notice of nonrenewal, consistent with C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b). The revised language reads: \"If we elect not to renew this policy, we will mail written notice of nonrenewal to the first Named Insured shown in the Declarations at least forty-five (45) days before the expiration date of this policy.\" The revised filing was submitted through SERFF on August 5, 2021.

**Disposition:** Approved by the Colorado Division of Insurance on August 20, 2021. No further objections were raised.

**Analyst Note:** This issue must be checked in any new Colorado filing. The 45-day nonrenewal notice requirement is a frequent source of filing objections for multi-state insurers who default to a 30-day notice period based on other states\' requirements. The new proprietary form MCP-2025-01 must be specifically verified against this requirement. I have included this as a checklist item in the Colorado Requirements Checklist.

**Cross-reference:** See Colorado Requirements Checklist, Item 12 --- Cancellation and Nonrenewal Provisions.

**Disposition of Filing MERI-2023-007 --- Wildfire Coverage Disclosure**

**Objection Received:** March 22, 2023

**Issue Identified:** The filed commercial property endorsement did not contain any wildfire-specific disclosure language. The Colorado Division of Insurance objected on the grounds that C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5 mandates that commercial property insurance policies include specific disclosure language regarding wildfire coverage, including information about wildfire sublimits, exclusions, deductibles, and coverage status. The Division noted that the inclusion of fire as a general covered peril does not satisfy the separate wildfire disclosure requirement.

**Corrective Action Taken:** A wildfire disclosure endorsement (Endorsement MCP-WF-01) was created and added to the filing. The endorsement included the following disclosure elements: (i) confirmation that wildfire losses are covered under the fire peril as a covered cause of loss; (ii) a statement that no separate wildfire sublimit applies unless specifically identified in the Declarations; (iii) a statement that no separate wildfire deductible applies unless specifically identified in the Declarations; and (iv) notice language printed in bold type informing the policyholder of their wildfire coverage status in plain language. The revised filing was submitted through SERFF on April 10, 2023.

**Disposition:** Approved by the Colorado Division of Insurance on April 28, 2023. No further objections were raised.

**Analyst Note:** Wildfire disclosure is a Colorado-specific requirement that is not found in most other states where we operate. The product development team in Chicago should be reminded of this requirement when drafting any new Colorado property form. I have flagged this in the Colorado Requirements Checklist under Item 8 --- Wildfire Coverage Disclosure. The new form MCP-2025-01 should either incorporate the wildfire disclosure directly into the policy form or require the WF-01 endorsement to be attached to every Colorado-issued policy.

**Additional Note:** I am concerned that the new proprietary form may not have adequately addressed this requirement --- I have not yet confirmed whether wildfire disclosure language was included in the draft of Form MCP-2025-01 that was circulated for internal review. The product development team drafted the form based primarily on the existing ISO CP 00 10 template and Meridian\'s internal coverage enhancements, and Colorado-specific disclosure requirements may not have been incorporated into the base form. This should be a priority item in the outside counsel review.

**Cross-reference:** See Colorado Requirements Checklist, Item 8 --- Wildfire Coverage Disclosure.

**General Note on Meridian\'s Colorado Filing History**

Meridian Casualty Insurance Company has filed fourteen (14) endorsements and form amendments with the Colorado Division of Insurance over the past five years (2020--2024). Of these fourteen filings, two were objected to by the Division --- Filing MERI-2021-003 and Filing MERI-2023-007, as documented above. Both objections were resolved through corrective filings, and the revised forms were approved. The remaining twelve filings were approved without objection.

Given that the new Form MCP-2025-01 is a fully proprietary commercial property coverage form replacing Meridian\'s existing ISO-based program, it represents a significantly larger regulatory risk than the individual endorsement filings that constitute Meridian\'s prior Colorado filing history. A proprietary base form encompasses all coverage provisions, conditions, exclusions, and regulatory compliance elements in a single document, and any issues found in prior endorsement filings may recur if the new form was drafted without specific reference to Colorado-specific requirements. The risk of recurrence is heightened by the fact that the product development team in Chicago may not have had access to, or awareness of, the Colorado-specific objection history when drafting the new form.

Outside counsel at Hargrove & Calloway LLP has been engaged (effective January 22, 2025) to perform an independent compliance review of Form MCP-2025-01 against all applicable Colorado regulatory requirements. These prior objection letters should be provided to Rebecca Sung at Hargrove & Calloway for her reference as part of the engagement materials. The filing target date for Form MCP-2025-01 is March 1, 2025, with submission to be made through Trenton Filing Services LLC via SERFF.

*End of Compiled Objection Correspondence --- MERI-2021-003 and MERI-2023-007* *Meridian Casualty Insurance Company --- Regulatory Filing Archive* *Compiled January 15, 2025 --- A. Brennan*

**[COLORADO REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS CHECKLIST]{.underline}**

**[Commercial Property Policy Form Filing]{.underline}**

**INTERNAL --- PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Field**                                       **Detail**
  ----------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Prepared By:**                                Alicia Brennan, Regulatory Filing Analyst, Meridian Casualty Insurance Company

  **Reviewed By:**                                David Kaminski, VP of Regulatory Compliance

  **Date Prepared:**                              January 15, 2025

  **Form Under Review:**                          Form MCP-2025-01 --- Meridian Commercial Property Coverage Form (Edition Date: January 2025)

  **Intended Filing Jurisdiction:**               State of Colorado --- Colorado Division of Insurance (Part of Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA))

  **Commissioner:**                               Michael R. Delacroix

  **Deputy Commissioner, Property & Casualty:**   Janet Winslow

  **Planned SERFF Tracking Number:**              MERI-133318601

  **Planned SERFF Filing Date:**                  March 1, 2025

  **Requested Effective Date:**                   April 15, 2025

  **Filing Agent:**                               Trenton Filing Services LLC
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Outside Counsel for Independent Review:**

> Hargrove & Calloway LLP
>
> Attn: Rebecca Sung, Associate
>
> 1750 Welton Street, Suite 400 Denver, CO 80202

**Engagement and Timeline Notes:**

This checklist is to be transmitted to outside counsel for an independent gap analysis pursuant to the engagement letter dated January 22, 2025. The scope of the engagement calls for outside counsel to review this checklist in conjunction with the complete text of Form MCP-2025-01, the prior objection letters referenced herein, and any additional Colorado statutory or regulatory requirements that may not be captured in this checklist. The target completion date for outside counsel\'s independent review and written gap analysis is February 7, 2025. Following receipt of outside counsel\'s analysis, the compliance team will prepare a revised version of Form MCP-2025-01, with a target completion date of February 14, 2025, in order to allow sufficient time for internal review and approval before the planned March 1, 2025 SERFF filing date.

All persons receiving this document are reminded that it was prepared at the direction of the VP of Regulatory Compliance and constitutes attorney work product prepared in anticipation of regulatory review. This document should not be distributed outside of the compliance team, the legal department, and outside counsel without prior authorization from the VP of Regulatory Compliance or General Counsel.

**[INSTRUCTIONS AND KEY TO STATUS FIELDS]{.underline}**

This checklist covers Colorado-specific statutory and regulatory requirements applicable to commercial property insurance policy forms. It is organized by statutory and regulatory citation, beginning with Colorado Revised Statutes (C.R.S.) sections and followed by Colorado Code of Regulations (3 CCR 702-4) provisions. Each requirement is assessed against the specific language of Form MCP-2025-01 --- Meridian Commercial Property Coverage Form (Edition Date: January 2025).

**Entry Format:** Each entry in this checklist contains four fields:

1\. **Citation** --- The specific statute or regulation reference.

2\. **Requirement Description** --- A plain-language summary of the mandate imposed by the cited authority.

3\. **Compliance Notes** --- Observations regarding whether Form MCP-2025-01 meets the stated requirement. Some entries contain detailed analysis; others are blank, partial, or marked as not yet reviewed. Entries marked as not yet reviewed require further analysis before the filing is submitted.

4\. **Status** --- One of the following designations:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Status**                          **Meaning**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Compliant                           Form MCP-2025-01 appears to satisfy the requirement based on current review.

  Potential Issue                     A concern has been identified that may or may not rise to the level of non-compliance; further analysis is needed.

  Non-Compliant                       Form MCP-2025-01 does not satisfy the requirement as currently drafted. Corrective action is required before filing.

  Not Yet Reviewed                    The requirement has not been fully analyzed. Analysis must be completed before the filing is submitted.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Completeness Disclaimer:** This checklist is thorough but may not be exhaustive of all Colorado requirements. It covers the principal Colorado-specific mandates for commercial property forms. Outside counsel should apply independent judgment and identify any requirements not captured here. The absence of a particular statute, regulation, or bulletin from this checklist should not be interpreted as confirmation that no such requirement exists.

**Cross-Reference to Prior Objections:** See prior objection letters for Filing MERI-2021-003 (July 2021, nonrenewal notice period deficiency) and Filing MERI-2023-007 (March 2023, wildfire disclosure deficiency). These prior objections should be given special attention to avoid recurrence. Copies of both objection letters and the corresponding corrective filings are maintained in the regulatory compliance files and will be provided to outside counsel under separate cover.

**Company Background:** Meridian Casualty Insurance Company, NAIC Code 29847, is domiciled in the State of Illinois. Meridian currently writes approximately \$47 million in annual Colorado commercial property premium. The target market for Form MCP-2025-01 is small-to-midsize commercial property risks with total insurable values (TIVs) ranging from \$500,000 to \$25,000,000. The form is a proprietary, company-developed form and is not based on Insurance Services Office (ISO) forms, although certain provisions are modeled on ISO CP 00 10 and related standard forms.

**[SECTION 1: CANCELLATION AND NONRENEWAL REQUIREMENTS (C.R.S. § 10-4-403 ET SEQ.)]{.underline}**

The following entries address the cancellation and nonrenewal requirements established under the Colorado Insurance Code. These requirements are among the most commonly cited bases for Division of Insurance objections to commercial property form filings, and Meridian has previously received an objection on this topic. Each entry addresses a specific provision of C.R.S. § 10-4-403.

**Entry 1.1 --- Cancellation Notice Period (C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(a))**

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(a)

**Requirement Description:** For commercial property policies, the insurer must provide at least forty-five (45) days\' written notice of cancellation when cancellation is for reasons other than nonpayment of premium. For cancellation due to nonpayment of premium, the insurer must provide at least ten (10) days\' written notice.

**Compliance Notes:** Form MCP-2025-01, Section VII, Condition 12 (\"Cancellation and Nonrenewal\") provides that the Company will mail written notice of cancellation at least forty-five (45) days before the effective date of cancellation when cancellation is for reasons other than nonpayment of premium, and at least ten (10) days before the effective date of cancellation when cancellation is due to nonpayment of premium. The form language tracks the statutory notice periods. This provision appears compliant on cancellation notice period.

**Status:** Compliant

**Entry 1.2 --- Nonrenewal Notice Period (C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b))**

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b)

**Requirement Description:** The insurer must provide at least forty-five (45) days\' advance written notice of nonrenewal of a commercial property policy before the policy expiration date. The notice must state the reason(s) for nonrenewal. This requirement applies regardless of the reason for nonrenewal and is not subject to any exception for nonrenewal at the insurer\'s discretion.

**Compliance Notes:** Form MCP-2025-01, Section VII, Condition 12 (\"Cancellation and Nonrenewal\") states that Meridian will mail written notice of nonrenewal \"at least 30 days before the expiration date of this policy.\" The statute requires forty-five (45) days. The form provides only thirty (30) days --- a fifteen (15) day shortfall. **NOTE: This exact issue was identified in Filing MERI-2021-003 (July 2021), which was objected to by the Colorado Division of Insurance. The objection letter specifically cited the 30-day vs. 45-day discrepancy under C.R.S. § 10-4-403(1)(b). The corrective endorsement filed in response to that objection extended the nonrenewal notice period to 45 days, and the refiled form was approved. However, Form MCP-2025-01 reverts to the deficient 30-day period. This must be corrected before filing to avoid a repeat objection.** The nonrenewal notice period in Section VII, Condition 12 must be revised from \"30 days\" to \"45 days\" to conform with the statute.

**Status:** Non-Compliant

**Entry 1.3 --- Reasons for Cancellation / Nonrenewal (C.R.S. § 10-4-403(2))**

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-403(2)

**Requirement Description:** Any notice of cancellation or nonrenewal of a commercial property policy must include the specific reason(s) for the insurer\'s action. The statute requires that the insured be informed of the basis for the insurer\'s decision, and a bare notice of cancellation or nonrenewal without stated reasons does not satisfy the requirement.

**Compliance Notes:** The form\'s cancellation and nonrenewal condition states that any notice of cancellation or nonrenewal \"will state the reason for cancellation or nonrenewal.\" This language appears to satisfy the statutory requirement that specific reasons be provided. The form does not limit or restrict the types of reasons that may be stated, which is appropriate.

**Entry 1.4 --- Cancellation Notice Delivery Method (C.R.S. § 10-4-403(4))**

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-403(4)

**Requirement Description:** Notice of cancellation or nonrenewal must be delivered by first-class mail to the policyholder\'s last known address, or by electronic means if the policyholder has affirmatively consented to electronic delivery in writing or through an electronic acknowledgment process. The statute specifies \"first-class mail\" as the required standard for physical mail delivery. Electronic delivery is permitted only when consent has been obtained through a qualifying process.

**Compliance Notes:** Form MCP-2025-01, Section VII, Condition 12 states that cancellation and nonrenewal notices will be sent by \"regular mail to the first Named Insured at the mailing address shown in the Declarations.\" Two issues have been identified with this language:

> \(1\) The form uses the term \"regular mail\" rather than the statutory term \"first-class mail.\" The term \"regular mail\" is ambiguous and could be interpreted to include less reliable delivery methods such as bulk mail or standard mail, which may not satisfy the statutory requirement. The form should be revised to use the term \"first-class mail\" to track the statutory language precisely.
>
> \(2\) The form does not include any provision for electronic delivery with policyholder consent, as permitted by the statute. While electronic delivery is not mandatory, the absence of an electronic delivery option may create operational issues and inconsistency with Meridian\'s current electronic delivery practices in other states. Both items should be addressed in the form revision.

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-105

**Requirement Description:** Colorado maintains statutory standard fire policy requirements. Any commercial property policy that provides fire coverage must include the standard provisions prescribed by statute or contain provisions that are at least as favorable to the insured as those prescribed. Key provisions include coverage for fire and lightning, certain minimum conditions regarding the insured\'s duties after loss, the insurer\'s obligations upon receipt of a claim, and mandatory provisions regarding concealment, fraud, and policy territory. Deviations from the standard fire policy provisions are permitted only if the deviation is at least as favorable to the insured.

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-105.2

**[SECTION 3: WILDFIRE COVERAGE DISCLOSURE (C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5)]{.underline}**

Wildfire disclosure requirements are a critical area of focus for Colorado commercial property filings. The Colorado Division of Insurance has been particularly attentive to wildfire-related requirements in recent years, reflecting the increasing severity and frequency of wildfire events in the state. Meridian has previously received an objection on this topic.

**Entry 3.1 --- Wildfire Coverage Disclosure Requirements (C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5)**

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5

**Requirement Description:** Commercial property insurance policies must include specific disclosure language regarding wildfire coverage, including:

> \(a\) A clear statement of whether wildfire is a covered peril under the policy;
>
> \(b\) Disclosure of any wildfire-specific sublimits, deductibles, or exclusions that apply to the policy;
>
> \(c\) A notice to the insured regarding wildfire risk if the covered property is located in a wildfire-prone area as designated by applicable Colorado or local fire authority maps; and
>
> \(d\) Information about available wildfire mitigation resources, including references to state-sponsored programs and resources that may assist the insured in reducing wildfire risk to the covered property.

This disclosure must be conspicuously placed in the policy form or provided as a mandatory accompanying notice delivered with the policy at inception and at each renewal. The statute does not permit the disclosure to be buried in general policy language or relegated to an optional endorsement.

**Compliance Notes:** Form MCP-2025-01 includes wildfire within the general fire peril coverage --- that is, fire from any cause, including wildfire, is a covered peril under the special causes of loss form, and no separate wildfire exclusion or sublimit is imposed. However, the form contains **no wildfire-specific disclosure language, notice, or information provisions** anywhere in its thirty-eight (38) pages. No mandatory accompanying notice regarding wildfire coverage has been drafted. The form does not include a statement regarding whether wildfire is a covered peril (even though it is), does not disclose the absence of wildfire-specific sublimits or deductibles, does not include a wildfire risk notice, and does not provide wildfire mitigation resource information. **NOTE: This exact issue caused the objection to Filing MERI-2023-007 (March 2023). The Colorado Division of Insurance objected because the form lacked mandatory wildfire coverage disclosure language required under C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5. A corrective wildfire disclosure endorsement was subsequently drafted, attached to the form, and the revised filing was approved. However, the current Form MCP-2025-01 does not incorporate this previously drafted disclosure language and no separate disclosure endorsement has been prepared for this proprietary form. A repeat deficiency on this point would be particularly problematic and could delay approval.** A wildfire disclosure provision must be added to the form or a mandatory wildfire disclosure notice must be prepared and included as a required attachment to the policy.

**Status:** Non-Compliant

**[SECTION 4: REPLACEMENT COST COVERAGE OFFER (C.R.S. § 10-4-110.4)]{.underline}**

Colorado requires that insurers affirmatively offer replacement cost coverage on commercial property policies. The purpose of this requirement is to ensure that commercial property policyholders are aware of the availability of replacement cost valuation and have the opportunity to elect or decline it, rather than being defaulted into actual cash value coverage without disclosure.

**Entry 4.1 --- Mandatory Offer of Replacement Cost Coverage (C.R.S. § 10-4-110.4)**

**Citation:** C.R.S. § 10-4-110.4

**Requirement Description:** Insurers must offer replacement cost coverage on commercial property policies. The offer must appear in the policy form itself or in a mandatory notice accompanying the policy at inception and at each renewal. The offer must be clear and conspicuous, allowing the insured to affirmatively elect or decline replacement cost coverage. Merely referencing an optional endorsement that may be available upon request, without providing a specific offer or disclosure of the availability and nature of replacement cost coverage, is insufficient to satisfy the statutory mandate. The purpose of the requirement is to ensure informed decision-making by the policyholder regarding valuation basis.

**Compliance Notes:** Form MCP-2025-01, Section V, Condition 3 (\"Valuation\") provides only actual cash value (ACV) as the default valuation basis for all covered property. The valuation condition states that \"the value of Covered Property will be determined at actual cash value as of the time of loss or damage.\" There is a brief reference in the form to an optional replacement cost endorsement: \"Replacement cost valuation may be attached by Endorsement MCP-RC-01.\" However, the form itself contains no language that constitutes an offer of replacement cost coverage to the insured. The reference to an optional endorsement does not include any description of what replacement cost coverage provides, does not explain how replacement cost valuation differs from actual cash value, and does not include any mechanism for the insured to affirmatively elect or decline replacement cost coverage. No mandatory accompanying notice offering replacement cost coverage has been drafted. The reference to an optional endorsement does not satisfy the statutory requirement --- the statute requires an affirmative offer in the policy form or in a mandatory notice accompanying the policy, not merely a passing reference to an endorsement that \"may be attached.\"

**Status:** Non-Compliant

**Entry 7.2 --- Coinsurance Clause Explanatory Language (Regulation 4-2-22)**

**Citation:** 3 CCR 702-4, Regulation 4-2-28

**Requirement Description:** Commercial property policies containing an appraisal provision must include a mechanism for umpire selection in the event the two party-appointed appraisers fail to agree on an umpire. **Corrective Action Taken:** Meridian drafted a wildfire disclosure endorsement that addressed each of the four required elements under C.R.S. § 10-4-110.5. The endorsement was attached to the form, and the revised filing was resubmitted and approved by the Division in June 2023.

**Current Form Status:** Form MCP-2025-01 does not include wildfire disclosure language. The previously drafted wildfire disclosure endorsement was specific to the prior form and has not been adapted or incorporated into this new proprietary form. No separate disclosure endorsement has been prepared. See Entry 3.1 above for full analysis. **THIS IS A CRITICAL ITEM. The wildfire disclosure must be incorporated into the form or a new mandatory disclosure endorsement must be prepared before the form is filed. A repeat objection on this issue would be particularly damaging to Meridian\'s credibility with the Division, especially given that the prior objection was signed by Deputy Commissioner Winslow, who remains in her position.**

**Status:** Readability testing has not yet been performed on Form MCP-2025-01. A readability certificate or test score must accompany the SERFF filing submission. **This is a filing prerequisite --- the form cannot be submitted to SERFF without the readability certificate.** Action item assigned to the compliance team. The readability testing must be completed before the March 1, 2025 filing date. If revisions are needed to meet readability standards, additional time will be required for plain-language revisions, internal review, and re-testing, which could potentially impact the filing timeline. Given the technical nature and length of the form (38 pages), early completion of readability testing is strongly recommended to allow time for any necessary revisions. Target completion: no later than February 15, 2025.

The following items must be completed, assembled, and reviewed before the filing package can be submitted via Trenton Filing Services LLC through SERFF:

>

>
> • \[ \] Certification of compliance signed by an authorized officer of Meridian Casualty Insurance Company
>
> • \[ \] Supporting documents, including prior filing history, copies of prior objection letters, and response letters demonstrating remediation of prior objections

**Filing Agent:** Trenton Filing Services LLC

**Deliverable:** Independent compliance gap analysis of Form MCP-2025-01 against Colorado statutory and regulatory requirements, incorporating review of this checklist, the complete policy form, and prior objection letters.

**Notes:** Outside counsel should review this checklist alongside the policy form and the prior objection letters. Any requirements not captured in this checklist should be independently identified and reported. This checklist is thorough but may not be exhaustive of all Colorado requirements that apply to commercial property forms. Outside counsel is expected to apply independent judgment, conduct independent research, and identify any gaps in this checklist that require correction or additional analysis.

**[MERIDIAN COMMERCIAL PROPERTY COVERAGE FORM]{.underline}**

**Meridian Casualty Insurance Company**

200 West Adams Street, Suite 3200 Chicago, Illinois 60606

NAIC Company Code: 29847

THIS POLICY FORM IS ISSUED BY MERIDIAN CASUALTY INSURANCE COMPANY, A STOCK PROPERTY AND CASUALTY INSURER DOMICILED IN THE STATE OF ILLINOIS. THIS FORM IS PART OF YOUR POLICY. PLEASE READ IT CAREFULLY. WORDS AND PHRASES THAT APPEAR IN BOLD HAVE SPECIAL MEANING. REFER TO SECTION VIII --- DEFINITIONS.

**[SECTION I --- DECLARATIONS PAGE TEMPLATE]{.underline}**

**[1.1 Named Insured and Address]{.underline}**

**First Named Insured**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

**Additional Named Insured(s)**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

**Mailing Address**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

**Physical Address of Insured Premises**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

**[1.2 Policy Period]{.underline}**

**Policy Period**: From: **\_\_\_\_ To: \_\_\_\_**

(12:01 a.m. Standard Time at the mailing address of the first **Named Insured** shown above.)

This policy applies to loss or damage that commences during the **policy period** shown above.

**[1.3 Agent / Broker Information]{.underline}**

**Agent Name**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

**Agent Address**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

**Agent License Number**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_**\_

**[1.4 Schedule of Coverages and Limits of Insurance]{.underline}**

The following Schedule shows the Coverages, Limits of Insurance, Covered Causes of Loss, and Coinsurance percentages applicable to this policy. Only those Coverages for which a Limit of Insurance is shown are applicable.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Coverage**                                           **Limit of Insurance**   **Covered Causes of Loss**                **Coinsurance %**
  ------------------------------------------------------ ------------------------ ----------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------
  **Coverage A --- Building**                            \$ **\_\_\_***\_*        Basic Broad Special                       80% 90% 100%

  **Coverage B --- Business Personal Property**          \$ **\_\_\_***\_*        Basic Broad Special                       80% 90% 100%

  **Coverage C --- Business Income and Extra Expense**   \$ **\_\_\_***\_*        Monthly Limit of Indemnity: \$ **\_\_**   Maximum Period of Restoration: **12 months**
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Deductible**: \$ **\_\_\_***\_* (Options: \$1,000 / \$2,500 / \$5,000 / \$10,000 / \$25,000 --- as selected)

**Valuation**: **Actual Cash Value**

The valuation basis applicable to all Covered Property under this policy is **Actual Cash Value** unless otherwise modified by endorsement attached to this policy. **Actual Cash Value** means the cost to replace the damaged property with property of like kind and quality, less a deduction for depreciation, physical wear and tear, and obsolescence. All loss adjustments will be made on the basis of **Actual Cash Value** unless an endorsement specifically providing for a different valuation method has been issued and attached to this policy.

**[1.5 Additional Coverages --- Schedule of Sublimits]{.underline}**

The following Additional Coverages are included in this policy, subject to the sublimits and terms stated below and further described in Section III:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Additional Coverage**             **Sublimit**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Ordinance or Law                    **10% of Coverage A Limit of Insurance**

  Debris Removal                      **25% of amount of direct physical loss or damage, subject to a maximum of \$250,000 per occurrence**

  Pollutant Cleanup and Removal       **\$25,000 aggregate per 12-month policy period**

**Endorsements attached to this policy at inception**: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_***\_*

*Optional endorsements that may be available include: Endorsement MCP-RC-01 (Replacement Cost Valuation), Endorsement MCP-AO-01 (Agreed Value), Endorsement MCP-EQ-01 (Earthquake), Endorsement MCP-FL-01 (Flood). The availability of optional endorsements may vary by state and underwriting eligibility. Consult your agent or broker for additional information regarding the availability of optional coverages.*

**[SECTION II --- INSURING AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**[2.1 Coverage Grant]{.underline}**

We will pay for direct physical loss of or damage to **Covered Property** at the **premises** described in the **Declarations**, caused by or resulting from a **Covered Cause of Loss**.

We will pay the **Actual Cash Value** of the **Covered Property** at the time of loss or damage, subject to the applicable Limit of Insurance, deductible, and the provisions of this Coverage Part. Payment under this Coverage Part shall in no event exceed the applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the **Declarations** for the type of **Covered Property** that has sustained the loss or damage.

Direct physical loss of or damage to **Covered Property** must occur during the **policy period** shown in the **Declarations**. Loss or damage that begins before the inception of this policy, even if it continues or worsens during the **policy period**, is not covered. Loss or damage that commences during the **policy period** but is not discovered until after the expiration of the **policy period** may be covered, provided that the loss or damage commenced during the **policy period** and the **Named Insured** complies with the duties described in Section VII, Condition 6 (Duties in the Event of Loss or Damage).

We have no duty to pay for loss or damage until we receive a satisfactory proof of loss from the **Named Insured** in accordance with the requirements of this Coverage Part. Our obligation to pay any claim is subject to all of the terms, conditions, limitations, and exclusions of this Coverage Part, including but not limited to the applicable deductible, coinsurance requirements, sublimits, and valuation provisions.

All adjustments and settlements under this Coverage Part will be made with the first **Named Insured** shown in the **Declarations**, unless otherwise directed in writing by the first **Named Insured**.

**[2.2 Covered Property]{.underline}**

**Covered Property**, as used in this Coverage Part, means the type of property described in this section at the **premises** described in the **Declarations**, for which a Limit of Insurance is shown in the **Declarations**. **Covered Property** includes property described under Coverage A (Building), Coverage B (Business Personal Property), and Coverage C (Business Income and Extra Expense), as applicable and as specifically described in Section III of this Coverage Part. Property that is not described in Coverage A, Coverage B, or Coverage C, or for which no Limit of Insurance is shown in the **Declarations**, is not **Covered Property** under this Coverage Part.

**[2.3 Property Not Covered]{.underline}**

**Covered Property** does not include any of the following:

> \(a\) Animals, unless boarded by others, or if owned by the **Named Insured**, only as **Stock** while inside the building described in the **Declarations**;
>
> \(b\) Automobiles held for sale, including automobiles held for lease, rental, or consignment;
>
> \(c\) Bridges, roadways, walks, patios, and other paved surfaces;
>
> \(d\) The cost of excavations, grading, backfilling, or filling;
>
> \(e\) Foundations of buildings, structures, machinery, or boilers if the foundations are below the lowest basement floor, or where there is no basement, below the surface of the ground;
>
> \(f\) Land (including land on which the property is located), water, growing crops, standing timber, and lawns;
>
> \(g\) Personal property while airborne or waterborne, except when such property is within a building at the described **premises**;
>
> \(h\) Pilings, piers, bulkheads, wharves, or docks;
>
> \(i\) Underground pipes, flues, or drains;
>
> \(j\) The cost to research, replace, or restore the information on valuable papers and records, including those that exist as electronic data, except as provided under the Additional Coverages in Section III. This limitation applies to the informational content of such materials, not to the blank value of the media on which the information is recorded;
>
> \(k\) Contraband, or property in the course of illegal transportation or trade;
>
> \(l\) Currency, money, notes, securities, accounts, bills, evidences of debt, letters of credit, and negotiable instruments of any kind, except as specifically provided under Additional Coverages in Section III.

The items listed above are not **Covered Property** regardless of whether they are owned by the **Named Insured**, are in the **Named Insured\'s** care, custody, or control, or are property of others for which the **Named Insured** may be liable.

**[SECTION III --- COVERAGES]{.underline}**

**[3.1 Coverage A --- Building]{.underline}**

If a Limit of Insurance is shown in the **Declarations** for Coverage A --- Building, **Covered Property** includes the **building** or structure described in the **Declarations**, including all of the following:

> \(a\) Completed additions to the **building**;
>
> \(b\) Fixtures, including outdoor fixtures, that are permanently attached to the **building** or its grounds;
>
> \(c\) Permanently installed machinery and equipment, including but not limited to heating, ventilating, air conditioning, plumbing, electrical, and elevator systems;
>
> \(d\) Personal property owned by the **Named Insured** that is used to maintain or service the **building** or its premises, including but not limited to fire extinguishing equipment, outdoor furniture, floor coverings, and appliances used for refrigerating, ventilating, cooking, dishwashing, or laundering;
>
> \(e\) If not covered by other insurance, materials, equipment, supplies, and temporary structures on the described **premises** or within 100 feet of the described **premises**, used for making additions, alterations, or repairs to the **building** or structure.

Coverage A also includes additions under construction, alterations, and repairs to the **building**, provided such additions, alterations, or repairs are not otherwise covered by a builder\'s risk policy or other similar insurance. Materials, supplies, and temporary structures on or within 100 feet of the described **premises** that are used for making such additions, alterations, or repairs are also included, but only if not covered by other insurance.

**Building** does not include land (including the land on which the **building** is located) or water. The term **building** does not include personal property as described in Coverage B, except to the extent that such personal property is specifically included in the definition of **building** as set forth above.

The Limit of Insurance for Coverage A applies to the total of all loss or damage to the **building** in any one **occurrence**, including loss or damage to all items described above that are part of the **building** as defined in this Coverage.

**[3.2 Coverage B --- Business Personal Property]{.underline}**

If a Limit of Insurance is shown in the **Declarations** for Coverage B --- Business Personal Property, **Covered Property** includes **business personal property** located in or on the **building** described in the **Declarations** or in the open (or in a vehicle) within 100 feet of the described **premises**, consisting of the following:

> \(a\) Property owned by the **Named Insured** and used in the **Named Insured\'s** business, including but not limited to furniture, fixtures, machinery, equipment, **stock**, and supplies;
>
> \(b\) Property of others that is in the **Named Insured\'s** care, custody, or control, except as otherwise provided in this Coverage Part. The **Named Insured\'s** obligation to pay for loss or damage to property of others is limited to the **Named Insured\'s** legal liability for such loss or damage, unless the **Named Insured** has assumed such liability by written contract;
>
> \(c\) Tenant\'s improvements and betterments, meaning fixtures, alterations, installations, or additions comprising a part of the **building** occupied by the **Named Insured** but not owned by the **Named Insured**, which were made or acquired at the expense of the **Named Insured** and which the **Named Insured** cannot legally remove;
>
> \(d\) Leased personal property for which the **Named Insured** has a contractual responsibility to insure, unless otherwise provided for under the terms of the lease agreement.

**Business personal property** does not include property that is specifically described as not covered under Section II, Paragraph 2.3 of this Coverage Part. The Limit of Insurance for Coverage B applies to the total of all loss or damage to **business personal property** in any one **occurrence**.

**[3.3 Coverage C --- Business Income and Extra Expense]{.underline}**

If a Limit of Insurance is shown in the **Declarations** for Coverage C --- Business Income and Extra Expense, the following provisions apply:

**Business Income.** We will pay for the actual loss of **Business Income** the **Named Insured** sustains due to the necessary suspension of **operations** during the **period of restoration**. The suspension must be caused by direct physical loss of or damage to property at the described **premises**, including personal property in the open (or in a vehicle) within 100 feet of the described **premises**, caused by or resulting from a **Covered Cause of Loss**.

**Business Income** means the sum of:

> \(a\) Net income (net profit or loss before income taxes) that would have been earned or incurred if no direct physical loss or damage had occurred; and
>
> \(b\) Continuing normal operating expenses incurred, including payroll.

The amount of **Business Income** loss will be determined based on the net income of the business before the direct physical loss or damage occurred, the likely net income of the business if no loss or damage had occurred (due consideration shall be given to the experience of the business before the loss and the probable experience thereafter had no loss occurred), the operating expenses, including payroll, necessary to resume **operations** with the same quality of service that existed just before the direct physical loss or damage, and other relevant sources of information, including the **Named Insured\'s** financial records and accounting procedures.

**Period of Restoration**

The **period of restoration** begins 72 hours after the time of direct physical loss or damage caused by or resulting from any **Covered Cause of Loss** at the described **premises** and ends on the earlier of:

> \(a\) The date when the property at the described **premises** should be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality; or
>
> \(b\) Twelve (12) months from the date of direct physical loss or damage.

The maximum **period of restoration** under this Coverage Part is **12 months**. The **period of restoration** does not include any increased period required due to the enforcement of any ordinance or law that regulates the construction, use, or repair of any property, or requires the tearing down of any property, except as specifically provided in the Additional Coverage for Ordinance or Law.

**Extra Expense.** We will pay necessary **Extra Expense** the **Named Insured** incurs during the **period of restoration** that the **Named Insured** would not have incurred if there had been no direct physical loss of or damage to property at the described **premises** caused by or resulting from a **Covered Cause of Loss**. **Extra Expense** means expense incurred:

> \(a\) To avoid or minimize the suspension of business and to continue **operations** at the described **premises** or at replacement premises or at temporary locations, including relocation expenses and costs to equip and operate the replacement or temporary locations;
>
> \(b\) To minimize the suspension of business if the **Named Insured** cannot continue **operations**; or
>
> \(c\) To repair or replace any property, but only to the extent it reduces the amount of loss that otherwise would have been payable under this Coverage.

**Extended Business Income**

If the necessary suspension of **operations** produces a **Business Income** loss payable under this Coverage, we will pay for the actual loss of **Business Income** the **Named Insured** incurs during the period that begins on the date property is actually repaired, rebuilt, or replaced and **operations** are resumed, and ends on the earlier of:

> \(a\) The date the **Named Insured** could restore its **operations**, with reasonable speed, to the level that would generate the **Business Income** amount that would have existed if no direct physical loss or damage had occurred; or
>
> \(b\) Thirty (30) consecutive calendar days after the date determined in paragraph (a) of the **period of restoration** definition.

Extended Business Income does not apply to loss of **Business Income** incurred as a result of unfavorable business conditions caused by the impact of the **Covered Cause of Loss** in the area where the described **premises** is located. Loss of **Business Income** must be caused by direct physical loss of or damage to property at the described **premises** caused by or resulting from a **Covered Cause of Loss**.

**[3.4 Additional Coverages]{.underline}**

The following Additional Coverages are included in this Coverage Part, subject to the sublimits and terms stated below. Unless otherwise stated, these Additional Coverages are subject to all other terms, conditions, limitations, and exclusions of this Coverage Part.

**(a) Debris Removal**

We will pay the **Named Insured\'s** expense to remove debris of **Covered Property** caused by or resulting from a **Covered Cause of Loss** that occurs during the **policy period**. The expenses will be paid only if they are reported to us in writing within 180 days of the date of direct physical loss or damage.

The most we will pay under this Additional Coverage is 25% of the amount of direct physical loss or damage paid under this policy for the **Covered Property** that has sustained the loss, subject to a maximum of **\$250,000 per occurrence**. This amount is included within the applicable Limit of Insurance.

However, if the sum of the direct physical loss or damage and the debris removal expense exceeds the applicable Limit of Insurance, or if the debris removal expense exceeds the amount payable under the 25% limitation, we will pay an additional amount of debris removal expense, not to exceed \$25,000, for each location described in the **Declarations**. This additional amount is payable in addition to the applicable Limit of Insurance.

**(b) Preservation of Property**

If it is necessary to move **Covered Property** from the described **premises** to preserve it from loss or damage by a **Covered Cause of Loss**, we will pay for any direct physical loss of or damage to that property while it is being moved or while temporarily stored at another location. This Additional Coverage applies for a period of up to 30 days from the date the property was first moved. This Additional Coverage does not change the applicable Limit of Insurance.

**(c) Fire Department Service Charge**

When the fire department is called to save or protect **Covered Property** from a **Covered Cause of Loss**, we will pay up to **\$5,000 per occurrence** for the **Named Insured\'s** liability for fire department service charges assumed by contract or agreement prior to loss, or required by local ordinance. The most we will pay under this Additional Coverage is \$5,000 per **occurrence**. This amount is included within, and not in addition to, the Limit of Insurance. No deductible applies to this Additional Coverage.

**(d) Pollutant Cleanup and Removal**

We will pay the **Named Insured\'s** expense to extract **pollutants** from land or water at the described **premises** if the discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape of the **pollutants** is caused by or results from a **Covered Cause of Loss** that occurs during the **policy period**. The expenses will be paid only if they are reported to us in writing within 180 days of the date on which the **Covered Cause of Loss** occurs.

The most we will pay under this Additional Coverage for the sum of all such expenses arising out of **Covered Causes of Loss** occurring during each separate 12-month period of this policy is **\$25,000 aggregate per 12-month policy period**. This amount is in addition to the applicable Limit of Insurance.

**(e) Increased Cost of Construction --- Ordinance or Law**

If a **Covered Cause of Loss** causes direct physical loss of or damage to **Covered Property** under Coverage A --- Building, we will pay for the increased cost of construction incurred to comply with the enforcement of any ordinance or law that regulates the construction or repair of the damaged **building** at the described **premises**. The most we will pay under this Additional Coverage is **10% of the applicable Coverage A Limit of Insurance**, but not more than \$500,000 per **occurrence**. This Additional Coverage does not apply to the cost of demolition or the value of the undamaged portion of the **building**. Coverage A.

**(f) Newly Acquired or Constructed Property**

If the **Named Insured** acquires new buildings or business personal property at locations other than the described **premises**, or if the **Named Insured** constructs additions to existing **buildings** at the described **premises**, we will pay for direct physical loss of or damage to such property caused by or resulting from a **Covered Cause of Loss**, subject to the following:

>
